steps.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: square RPG vehicle portrait.
Create a recognizable M1A1 Abrams, stationary and unoccupied on a quiet broken asphalt road with dry weeds and gravel. Image 1 is a public-domain US Marine Corps M1A1 reference for the actual vehicle proportions and shape. Image 2 is ONLY the established painting style: detailed realistic hand-painted post-apocalyptic tabletop artwork, restrained rust, chipped paint and fine material detail.
Elevated front-left three-quarter view, front toward lower left; the ENTIRE tank, both track runs, complete long barrel and bustle rack fit inside the square with clear margin. Faded desert-tan paint, dust and modest wear, mechanically intact.
Keep the M1A1 identity: wide low hull; seven road wheels per side under slab side skirts; large angular wedge-front turret; broad rectangular rear turret bustle and empty stowage basket; long thermal-sleeved barrel with fume-extractor bulge and a plain cylindrical muzzle without a muzzle brake. Single centered driver hatch in the front hull, commander on vehicle-right and loader on vehicle-left of the turret. All hatches CLOSED. This is the M1A1, without the large round independent thermal viewer of the M1A2. Empty small roof mounts, no added roof machine guns, no people, no flags, insignia, numbers, lettering or watermark. Muted daylight, calm parked vehicle, no action, smoke or explosions.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct only the turret ROOF fittings on this parked M1A1 Abrams portrait. Keep the composition, long barrel, wedge-shaped turret armor, hull, seven-wheel tracks, weathered sand paint and roadside unchanged.
The current roof incorrectly resembles a crowded Bradley roof. Replace the TWO tall square periscope boxes on the turret roof with the proper low-profile Abrams arrangement: one flat closed loader hatch on the near side (vehicle-left), and a single closed circular commander's cupola on the far side (vehicle-right). Keep one low, small rectangular primary sight just forward of the commander's position. The gunner sits lower in the turret, not in a third raised box. Do NOT add any third crew hatch, extra tower or independent thermal viewer. Keep the empty rear bustle stowage basket and low rear roof panels. Make this a restrained classic M1A1 roof rather than an M1A2 modernization. No people, writing or extra equipment. Preserve the rest of the picture.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Make one small correction to the two roof hatch positions in this M1A1 portrait. Preserve the entire tank, all armor, barrel, tracks, paint and scene.
Swap the SHAPES of the two existing turret crew hatches, retaining their current centers and low heights:
- The hatch currently at the LEFT side of the image roof (approximately x54%, y27% of the image) should be the low CIRCULAR commander's cupola with small vision blocks.
- The hatch currently at the RIGHT side of the image roof (approximately x71%, y26%) should be the FLAT D-shaped loader's hatch, almost flush with the roof.
The small rectangular optics box forward of the hatches stays in place. Exactly two turret crew hatches, no extra tower. No people, text or other additions. This corrects the crew sides for the visible front-left viewpoint.

Use case: sketch-to-render. Asset type: transparent orthographic RPG token, M1A1 Abrams, roof and upper turret removed.
Image 1 is the authoritative geometry plan. Paint that plan with the realistic detailed style and weathered desert-tan exterior of image 2. The FRONT faces DOWN. Rear turbine deck is TOP. Strictly overhead, no perspective. Both tracks and the entire hull are visible, with genuine transparent background; no people, text, ground or cast shadow.
Preserve exactly FOUR distinct empty crew positions at the plan coordinates:
1. A centered reclined DRIVER seat in the front hull at the bottom, with small steering handlebars.
2. COMMANDER seat at image-left rear of the turret basket, behind the gunner.
3. GUNNER seat at image-left front of the turret basket.
4. LOADER's fold-down perch/work position on image-right of the turret basket.
There are exactly THREE crew positions in the circular basket, not three abreast and not four there. A compact central gray breech lies between the loader and gunner. Keep the large rear engine grille covered, and the front side storage covers closed. Interior pale gray-green metal, dark olive seat cushions, clear readable seat shapes. No passenger cabin or rear troop seats.
Remove ALL upper turret armor, roof fittings, hatch covers, upper hull cover over the driver, and external barrel, exposing the basket ring and all four crew positions. Keep lower side armor and tracks. Hull about 7.93 m long by 3.65 m wide. The blank lower end of the guide reserves space for the future barrel overhang: do not stretch the hull to fill that blank space. This is an empty gameplay cutaway, with realistic proportions governed by the drawing.

Follow the drawing's four empty places exactly: one seat centered at the front/bottom, two seats arranged one behind the other along image-left inside the circular middle compartment, and one perch at image-right of that compartment. Paint the flat top-assembly shapes of image 1 as a finished M1A1 Abrams tabletop miniature illustration. Image 1 is the exact geometry guide, image 2 is the matching finished open-top hull to preserve, image 3 is the vehicle portrait for the recognizable wedge-front Abrams shape and worn sand-colored paint.
Strict orthographic overhead view, FRONT DOWN. Genuine transparent background, complete long front projection in frame, no ground, people, text or action.
Keep the chassis, two tracks, rear engine grille, side skirts and front hull aligned to image 2. Replace only the guide's flat top shapes with detailed painted metal.
Preserve the guide positions: the closed circular commander's cupola is on image-left, centered about x36.5%, y36.7%; the closed flat loader hatch is on image-right, x66.3%, y41.7%. Exactly TWO crew hatches on the turret. The small low sight box farther forward on image-left is not another raised hatch. The centered driver hatch is in the front hull, below the long front projection.
Large angular Abrams turret, broad rear bustle with empty stowage basket toward the TOP; long thermal-sleeved barrel follows the guide toward BOTTOM, with its wider sleeve section and plain cylindrical tip. No extra towers or M1A2 thermal viewer, no added roof guns. Preserve the guide's exact frame, scale and proportions. Detailed realistic RPG painting, dusty chipped desert-tan metal, readable surfaces.
